test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), which major activity did the Reserve Bank of India mandate during July–September 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Re-KYC of accounts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **Government of India** have mandated the **Re-KYC (Know Your Customer)** process for **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)** accounts to ensure they remain compliant with current regulatory standards.
 
• Since **PMJDY** was launched in **August 2014**, a vast majority of the accounts have reached the **10-year** mark. According to **RBI guidelines**, periodic updation of **KYC** documents for **low-risk** customers must be carried out at least once every **10 years**.
 
• The mandated activity for the **July-September 2025** period involves banks reaching out to account holders to update their **identity** and **address proofs** to prevent these accounts from becoming **inoperative** or restricted.
 
• Banks have been instructed to use various methods for this process, including **self-declaration** (if there is no change in information), **Video-Based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP)**, **ATMs**, and **Mobile Banking** to minimize inconvenience to the account holders. ***Hence, the mandate for Re-KYC of accounts is correct.***
 
• This drive is essential for maintaining the **integrity** of the financial system and ensuring that **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** credits continue to reach the intended beneficiaries without technical glitches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY):**

 
 
• Launched on **August 28, 2014**, it is a **National Mission for Financial Inclusion** aimed at providing affordable access to financial services like **savings accounts**, **remittance**, **credit**, **insurance**, and **pensions**.
 
• It allows for the opening of **Basic Savings Bank Deposit (BSBD)** accounts with **zero balance** requirements, ensuring that even the poorest sections of society can access banking.
 
 
 
• **Key Features and Benefits:**
 
 
• Every account holder is provided with a **RuPay Debit Card**.
 
• Accounts opened after **August 28, 2018**, come with an enhanced **Accident Insurance Cover** of **Rs. 2 lakh** (it was **Rs. 1 lakh** for accounts opened before this date).
 
• An **Overdraft (OD)** facility of up to **Rs. 10,000** is available to eligible account holders, particularly targeting the **lady of the household** to promote **financial empowerment**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of KYC:**
 
 
• **KYC** is a process used by financial institutions to verify the identity and suitability of their clients. It is crucial for preventing **money laundering**, **identity theft**, and **financial fraud**.
 
• Under the **Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002**, banks are legally obligated to maintain updated records of their customers.
 
 
 
• **Inoperative Accounts:**
 
 
• A **PMJDY** account is treated as **inoperative** if there are no customer-induced transactions in the account for over **two years**. Regular **re-KYC** helps in identifying active versus dormant accounts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Official Documents (OVDs):** For the **re-KYC** process, customers can use any of the six **Officially Valid Documents**: **Aadhaar Card**, **Voter ID**, **Passport**, **Driving License**, **MNREGA Job Card**, or **PAN Card**.
 
• **Financial Inclusion Progress:** As of **2024**, more than **50 crore** PMJDY accounts have been opened with total deposits exceeding **Rs. 2 lakh crore**, signifying the massive scale of this **financial inclusion** initiative in **India**.
 
• **Digital Push:** The **RBI** has emphasized that if a customer has already submitted their **Aadhaar** and there is no change in their **residential address**, they should not be required to visit the branch physically for **re-KYC**.
